title: Correctness implies true claims
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $A$ be a Boolean answer table for state and tape-symbol queries indexed by two natural numbers. Fix a width $W$, time $t$, indices $a,j$, and a Boolean $b$. Suppose that at time $t$, the table answers every state-and-output query exactly according to the machine's configuration, and answers every work-tape query at signed offset $d$ correctly whenever $|d|+t\le 2^W-1$, as well as every input query whenever $|d|\le |x|+1$; also suppose $t<2^W$. Then the numerical valuation determined by $A,W,|x|,t,a,j,b$ makes the state-and-read claims at time $t$ true for the machine's actual configuration.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols
Correct state-and-output answers at time $t$ for every state-output pair
Correct work-tape answers for all offsets with $|d|+t\le 2^W-1$
Correct input answers for all offsets with $|d|\le |x|+1$
